commentary.text: I’m claiming a central square immediately with Red, establishing the first half of a potential Red–Yellow center formation while keeping open files for Yellow’s later approach.
I’m claiming a central square early while keeping open lanes for Green to help complete a center occupation.

Yellow joins Red in the center at (4,3), securing both lower central squares. The Blue piece at (3,3) prevents an immediate center win, so the next objective is to contest or capture it while protecting this formation.

I’m staging Green directly above the open central square at (3,4). Red and Yellow cannot enter that square through column 4 while their own Red piece blocks (4,4), so this creates a strong center claim for Green’s next turn.

I’m shifting Red to (3,4), occupying the remaining open upper-center square and preparing Yellow to refill (4,4) from the bottom edge. This keeps pressure on Blue at (3,3) and advances the center-win formation.

Red’s move created an immediate sandwich threat against the Blue center piece. I’m sliding it to (3,2), preserving it as a future Blue flank while leaving room to establish another Blue on the opposite side of Red.
Yellow fills (4,4), giving Team A three central squares. Red can complete the center next turn by moving from (0,3) to the open (3,3).
Team A is one central square from winning, and Red could otherwise enter (3,3) straight down column 3. I’m shifting Green to (2,3) to block that route and keep the center contest alive.

The direct descent to (3,3) is blocked by Green at (2,3). I’m repositioning the Red from (0,3) to (0,4), preparing a replacement on the (3,4) center square after the current central Red shifts left to (3,3).
Yellow can win immediately next turn by moving from (4,3) into the last open central square. Blue therefore returns to (3,3), occupying that square and denying the center completion.

I’m advancing a spare Yellow to (5,5) without disturbing the center. The key threat remains Red’s (0,2)→(3,2), which would sandwich and capture Blue at (3,3) against Red at (3,4); watch whether Green blocks that route.
Blue at (3,3) is threatened by a Red sandwich: Red could descend column 2 to (3,2), using Red at (3,4) as the far flank. Green moves to (2,2) to block that descent.

I’m staging Red at (3,1). Next Red turn it can slide to (3,2), sandwiching Blue at (3,3) against Red at (3,4); if Blue vacates the center, Red may instead occupy (3,3) once Green’s reply is accounted for.

I’m bringing a second Blue onto row 3. Green can occupy (3,2) next to stop Red’s immediate sandwich, while this Blue threatens to approach from the right and capture the Red piece at (3,4) against Blue’s central flank.

Yellow is staging on (2,6) for a second route to remove Blue’s central piece: if the lane remains open, Yellow can later land on (2,3) and sandwich Blue at (3,3) against Yellow at (4,3). This also restricts the Blue piece on (2,7) while preserving all three Team A center occupants.

Green’s defensive block is also a capture: landing on (3,2) sandwiches Red at (3,1) against the Green piece at (3,0). This removes the immediate threat to central Blue while inflicting Red’s first loss.

I’m evacuating the central Red to (1,4), avoiding Blue’s sandwich threat from the right while keeping a clear return route. Yellow can capture Blue whether it remains at (3,3) or shifts to (3,4), using the matching lower-center Yellow as the far flank.
Red has abandoned (3,4), so Blue can now secure both upper central squares. This denies Team A’s center threat and gives us half of a potential center-occupation win.

Yellow executes the prepared vertical sandwich: moving to (2,4) captures Blue on (3,4) against Yellow at (4,4). This removes Blue’s central blocker while preserving both lower-center Yellow pieces; Red can now reclaim an upper central square on its next turn.
I’m developing Green to (6,6), where it can later rise to (5,6) as a far flank against Yellow at (5,5). That would let the Green piece on row 5 approach from the left and complete a sandwich.

I’m staging Red at (3,5) while preserving the Red at (1,4). Yellow still threatens to capture Blue at (3,3) via (2,4)→(2,3); this new Red provides a useful right-side anchor if Blue shifts toward (3,4), and can later step into the upper center.
I’m restoring Blue’s right-side presence on row 3. If Yellow enters (3,4) while Red remains at (3,5), Blue can step to (3,6) and sandwich both pieces against the Blue at (3,3).
Yellow removes Blue’s last central blocker with the prepared sandwich against Yellow at (4,3). This opens (3,3) for Red while preserving Team A’s three-piece central structure.

Yellow’s capture opened a two-move center threat: Red could take (3,4), followed by Yellow taking (3,3). Green crosses into (3,4) now, blocking that sequence and claiming a central square for our team.

I’m staging Red at (1,3) so that after Yellow moves (2,3)→(2,4) to sandwich Green on (3,4), Red can descend through the cleared file to (3,3) and complete center occupation. Blue may try to block (2,4), so preserve the central Yellow pair and adapt if it does.

I’m placing Blue at (2,4) beside Yellow’s advanced piece. It is not immediately sandwichable, adds support near the center, and begins creating pressure along row 2 without exposing Blue to a third loss.

Yellow vacates the third file while staying nearby, opening Red’s route from (1,3) to (3,3). If Blue does not interpose, that Red move will sandwich Green at (3,4) against Red at (3,5), setting up the final center occupation.

Red is threatening to descend from (1,3) to (3,3) and sandwich the Green at (3,4) against Red at (3,5). I’m filling (3,3) with the second Green, denying that landing square and giving us both upper central squares.

I’m closing Yellow’s capture route by moving Blue onto (2,3). Yellow can no longer land there to sandwich Green at (3,3), while the Green at (3,4) blocks Yellow’s alternative approach through column 4.

Yellow clears Red’s second-file route by shifting to (2,1). If Green does not occupy (3,2), Red can land there next turn and sandwich both central Green pieces against Red at (3,5), reopening the center.
The Green staged on column 6 now has a direct tactical shot: moving to (3,6) sandwiches Red at (3,5) against Green at (3,4). This gives Red its second loss and leaves it one capture from elimination.
I’m preserving the center fight while making a safe corrective move with Red’s untouched top-edge reserve, shifting it into the open corner.
Red is one loss from elimination. I’m placing Blue at (1,4) as the right flank beside Red at (1,3), setting up a potential Blue sandwich from (1,2) and forcing Red to respect that threat.
I’m staging Yellow at (2,5), creating an immediate threat to move to (2,4) and sandwich Green at (3,4) against Yellow at (4,4). If Green evacuates, it voluntarily opens an upper central square.
Green can now attack the center directly. Moving to (5,3) sandwiches Yellow at (4,3) against the Green at (3,3), removing one of Team A’s central occupants and giving Yellow its first loss.

I’m staging Red at (4,2), creating a direct threat to step into (4,3) and vertically sandwich Green at (3,3) plus Blue at (2,3) against Red at (1,3). Meanwhile, Yellow at (2,5) can capture Green at (3,4), giving Team A coordinated routes to clear both upper central squares.

Green is poised to sandwich Yellow at (4,4) from below, so I’m developing Blue to (4,7). This narrows Yellow’s horizontal space and positions Blue on the same row for continued pressure if Yellow flees.

Yellow executes the prepared sandwich, landing at (2,4) to capture Green at (3,4) against Yellow at (4,4). This clears one upper-center square and leaves Red’s staged piece at (4,2) threatening entry into (4,3), while Red at (1,3) remains aligned against the pieces on the third file.

Yellow removed the upper Green flank, so I’m rebuilding the sandwich vertically. Green moves beneath Yellow at (4,4); next, the Green on row 3 can land at (3,4) and capture that Yellow piece against this new far flank.

Red springs the prepared vertical sandwich from (4,3), capturing Green at (3,3) and Blue at (2,3) against Red at (1,3). This eliminates Blue and clears the left central column, leaving Team A occupying both lower center squares and needing to reclaim the two upper ones.

Blue has been eliminated, so its pieces are now Void and cannot capture, but they still count toward a center win. I’m moving a Void Blue closer to the center, where it can help occupy or restrict the lower-right central lane after Yellow moves.
Yellow occupies (3,4), restoring three Team A center squares. Green has no direct route to block (3,3), so Red at (1,3) is poised to descend there next turn and complete the center victory.
I’m advancing Green beside Red at (1,3), restricting its horizontal movement and preserving the remaining Green pieces while applying pressure from the left.
Red descends into (3,3), completing Team A’s occupation of all four central squares and winning immediately by center occupation.
